Pull request overview
This PR updates CoreCLR’s async-variant method lookup so that ReturnDroppingThunk (RDT) methods can be distinguished from “regular” async variants during FindOrCreateAssociatedMethodDesc / instantiated-method-desc hashtable lookups, preventing incorrect matches when multiple async-kind variants share the same method identity apart from async kind.
Changes:

Adds AsyncVariantLookup::ReturnDroppingThunk plus MethodDesc::GetAsyncVariantLookup() and updates matching logic (MatchesAsyncVariantLookup) to disambiguate regular async variants vs RDTs.
Widens instantiated-method-desc lookup APIs from bool isAsyncVariant to AsyncVariantLookup and updates call sites accordingly.
Modifies the covariant-return async test by removing an ActiveIssue skip annotation on TestGenericVirtualMethod.

Pull request overview
Refactors String.Substring’s shared throw helper so it no longer captures this, by making the helper static and passing the string length explicitly. This is intended to make the calling code more amenable to JIT escape analysis without changing observable exception behavior.
Changes:

Update Substring(int startIndex) and Substring(int startIndex, int length) to pass Length into the throw helper.
Change ThrowSubstringArgumentOutOfRange from instance to static and use the passed-in length for bounds checks.

Pull request overview
This PR adjusts late (post-LSRA) block-flipping in the CoreCLR JIT to avoid creating new IR nodes after LIR has been formed, by introducing an in-place-only condition reversal helper. This prevents LIR integrity failures when condition reversal would otherwise require synthesizing new IR (e.g., wrapping a non-compare in == 0) and also handles GT_COPY/GT_RELOAD wrappers introduced by LSRA on GT_JTRUE operands.
Changes:

Add Compiler::gtTryReverseCond(GenTree*) -> bool to reverse supported conditions in-place (relops, JCC/SETCC, JCMP/JTEST, integral constants) without allocating new IR.
Make gtReverseCond a thin wrapper that preserves existing behavior by falling back to creating GT_EQ(tree, 0) when in-place reversal isn’t possible.
Update optOptimizePostLayout to (1) peel GT_COPY/GT_RELOAD off GT_JTRUE operands and (2) skip flipping a block when in-place reversal isn’t possible, rather than mutating LIR.

Pull request overview
Copilot reviewed 1 out of 1 changed files in this pull request and generated no new comments.

I verified this empirically rather than by inspection, and the fix is correct. Notes below — none of them blocking.
Verification
The diagnosis is right. MSBuild runs DependsOnTargets before BeforeTargets. Minimal repro:
== Dep1  →  == Dep2  →  == Before1 (BeforeTargets)  →  == Main

So BeforeTargets="GenerateNuspec" scheduled the target after the entire GenerateNuspec dependency chain, including _CalculateInputsOutputsForPack → _GetOutputItemsFromPack.
The fix works. I simulated the real pack target graph (GenerateNuspecDependsOn as built at lines 32/55/59 of NuGet.Build.Tasks.Pack.targets, plus GenerateNuspec DependsOnTargets="$(GenerateNuspecDependsOn);_CalculateInputsOutputsForPack;…"):




what _GetOutputItemsFromPack sees




before (BeforeTargets="GenerateNuspec")
NuspecProperties='' ❌


after (GenerateNuspecDependsOn)
NuspecProperties='PackageId=Foo;Version=1.2.3' ✅



Import-order robust. NuGet appends $(GenerateNuspecDependsOn) at the tail of its own list and prepends Build;, so this lands last in the list but still strictly before _CalculateInputsOutputsForPack — regardless of whether Workarounds.targets is imported before or after the pack targets.
Moving the target earlier is safe within Arcade. Everything it reads (PackageDescription, PackageLicenseFullPath, PackageIconFullPath, PackageVersion, …) is set at evaluation time in ProjectDefaults.props/.targets; the only target-produced values (RepositoryUrl/RepositoryCommit) come from its own DependsOnTargets. It also matches Pack.targets:5, which already uses this pattern — final chain ends …;InitializeStandardNuspecProperties;_ValidationSymbolPackageFormat, both still ahead of _CalculateInputsOutputsForPack.
Two things not covered by the inline comments
Necessary but not sufficient — worth saying so in the PR body. Per the aspnetcore investigation, GetPackOutputItemsTask unconditionally overwrites packageId with nuspecReader.GetId() whenever NuspecFile != ''. Arcade's $CommonMetadataElements$ composite token means the .nuspec has no literal <id> element, so GetId() returns empty and you get an output path like .11.0.0-dev.nupkg. This PR fixes only the version half. Please state that here and link a NuGet.Client issue so nobody assumes this unblocks aspnetcore on its own.
No regression coverage. There is no project in this repo using NuspecFile or NuspecPackageId, so green CI proves nothing about this code path and it can silently regress again. A scenario test that packs with a NuspecFile + $CommonMetadataElements$ and asserts the emitted nupkg name would be worth it — the "right tests are in" checkbox is still unchecked.

Holistic Review
Motivation: The problem is real and well-scoped: a new()-constrained generic attribute failed to keep its argument's parameterless constructor, and the trimmer could NRE while emitting IL2091 for generic-argument dataflow on a custom-attribute generic argument that has no resolvable declaring type/method. Both are legitimate correctness bugs.
Approach: The fix is minimal and consistent with existing patterns. Running ProcessGenericArgumentDataFlow for custom-attribute constructor types (guarded by RequiresGenericArgumentDataFlow) mirrors how method/field/interface dataflow is already handled, and the null-safety additions in DiagnosticUtilities/MemberReferenceExtensions are defensive fallbacks for the orphan-generic-parameter case. The C#-inexpressible scenario (CS8968) is correctly covered via a compiled-before IL dependency.
Summary: ⚠️ Needs Human Review. The code changes look correct and the crash/NRE and new()-constraint fixes are well-tested. However, the PR self-documents an incomplete approach: reviewers explicitly requested that the annotated generic-attribute argument produce no IL2091 warning, but the PR leaves annotated and unannotated arguments warning identically and only tests the unannotated (warning) case. A trimmer maintainer should decide whether shipping the partial fix (crash avoidance + correct warning for the unannotated case) is acceptable now, or whether the annotated-suppression half must land together. See Detailed Findings.
Detailed Findings
⚠️ Completeness — Annotated generic-attribute argument still warns (IL2091)
The PR description states the reviewer-requested "no warning when the argument is annotated" behavior is not achieved: a custom-attribute generic argument is encoded as an orphan positional generic parameter (!0, with DeclaringType/DeclaringMethod/Owner all null), so FlowAnnotations.GetGenericParameterAnnotation returns None and annotated/unannotated arguments warn identically. The added test (ReflectOnGenericAttributeWithUnannotatedTypeParameter + GenericAttributesDataFlow.il) only exercises the unannotated → warns path. This is a code-correct-but-approach-incomplete situation: it prevents the crash and warns correctly for the unannotated case, but does not deliver the annotated-suppression behavior a reviewer asked for, and there is no regression test asserting the (currently wrong) annotated case, so the gap is not tracked in CI. A human should decide whether to accept the partial fix or require the positional-generic-parameter resolution work before merge.
✅ Null-safety fallback in DiagnosticUtilities — no baseline regression
GetGenericParameterDeclaringMemberDisplayName now returns genericParameter.Name only when both DeclaringMethod and DeclaringType are null — precisely the orphan case that previously threw an NRE. All pre-existing paths (declaring type/method non-null) still call GetDisplayName() and are unchanged, so existing IL2091/related message baselines are not affected. (This addresses the concern raised by an earlier automated reviewer that the change would shorten display names generally — it does not.)
✅ Guarded dataflow call — correct and allocation-conscious
Guarding the new ProcessGenericArgumentDataFlow call with RequiresGenericArgumentDataFlow(...) avoids constructing a DiagnosticContext/ReflectionMarker and the requires-suppression check for the common non-generic-attribute case, matching the pattern used at the other RequireDynamicallyAccessedMembersAction/ReflectionMethodBodyScanner call sites.
💡 Test wiring — LogContains vs ExpectedWarning
Using [LogContains("IL2091.*ClassWithUnannotatedTypeParameter", regexMatch: true)] is the right choice here because the warning origin is the IL dependency assembly rather than the test assembly (where ExpectedWarning matches). This is sound, but note the assertion is looser than an origin-anchored ExpectedWarning — acceptable given the cross-assembly constraint.
NoteThis review was generated by this repository's Holistic Review agentic workflow to complement the built-in Copilot review.

Review of the workspace switcher scroll fix.
Method: 13 review agents across two waves, then three adversarial reviewers to adjudicate the contested claims. The two load-bearing claims below were settled by direct measurement in Chromium (a reconstruction of the CurrentUserButton -> PrimeVue Popover -> CurrentUserPopoverWorkspace -> nested absolute panel chain using primevue 4.2.5's real absolutePosition() algorithm and the design system's actual body rule) rather than by reading CSS, so the numbers are reproducible.
Note on scope: the matrix de-duplication you pushed as 2462408 dissolved most of the CI findings this review started with (the duplicated ~90 line staging block, the separate unsharded job, and the fifth needs: gate on merge-and-commit are all gone). Only the mobile-safari gap below survives from that group.
Two things worth your attention before merge, both cheap to close:

The E2E regression test passes against the unfixed component, so it does not currently gate this fix.
The bound landed on the inner list rather than the panel root, so at the cloud project's own 1280x720 viewport the create-workspace footer is 11px visible out of 48px.

Fixing (2) is what makes (1)'s replacement assertions meaningful, so they are best done together.
Out of scope, flagging separately rather than as a comment on this PR: pr-update-playwright-expectations.yaml:398-399 interpolates the PR branch name unquoted into git push, inside a job that holds PR_GH_TOKEN with persist-credentials: true. Branch names may legally contain backtick, $(), ; and | (confirmed locally with git check-ref-format, and by GitHub's own untrusted-input guidance; cf. GHSL-2023-100). Reachable via the issue_comment /update-playwright path. The same defect exists at pr-update-website-screenshots.yaml:120. This is pre-existing code that your diff does not touch (this PR's only edit to that job was the needs: list, now reverted), so it should not block a popover fix. Say the word and I will open a standalone security issue covering both call sites with the env: passthrough fix.
Disclosure: the adversarial pass was intended to run cross-model, but could not. run-headless-review.sh was calling codex exec -q, a flag removed in codex-cli 0.130.0, with stderr sent to /dev/null, so it had been silently falling through to the same model. I fixed the script; codex then reported no API credits remaining, and gemini/qwen are not installed. The adversarial reviewers therefore ran same-model, which is why the two claims above were settled by measurement instead of judgment.

Pull request overview
This PR aims to stop HeroDevs NES-only Spring BOM coordinates from leaking into published Maven artifacts by (1) re-importing Spring BOMs at the camunda-library-parent level so property overrides actually take effect, and (2) publishing flattened POMs for snapshot deployments to remove parent-chain BOM imports from consumer-visible descriptors.
Changes:

Re-import spring-boot-dependencies and spring-framework-bom (plus supporting BOM re-imports) in library-parent/pom.xml so managed versions resolve to OSS coordinates.
Adjust camunda-spring-boot-4-starter dependency management to override Jackson versions for the Spring Boot 4 line.
Update the snapshot deploy workflow to deploy flattened POMs (-Dflatten.updatePomFile=true) to match the release publish path.

Workflow validation notes (ci-validation skill)

workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml
tier: 3
reason: Uses self-hosted runners + Vault secrets + multi-job release/snapshot deployment logic, which is not realistically act-testable locally.
evidence: tier-3 rationale — validate via actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml + conftest test --rego-version v0 -o github --policy .github .github/workflows/*.yml + ./mvnw spotless:apply -T1C

Pull request overview
This PR updates the release-latest GitHub Actions workflow to prevent downstream post-publish steps from running until all newly published workspace package versions are actually resolvable on the npm registry (accounting for npm’s publish-time scanning hold).
Changes:

Adds a post-publish gating step that enumerates non-private workspace packages and polls npm view <name>@<version> until each version resolves or a timeout occurs.
Fails the npm-publish job with a clear list of still-missing packages if the registry does not serve them within the configured time window.

L1 — Low risk (dep bumps, docs/copy, lockfiles, small presentational fixes). buildsworth may approve by default.

L3 — High risk (auth, migrations, payments, secrets, perf-critical paths). Human review always required.
